items.label: lem:torsion
items.title: Torsion and lines
items.tex:
\begin{lemma}[Torsion and lines]\label{lem:torsion}
Let $p\mid n$ be prime. The following hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The $p$-torsion $\A[p]=\{\mathbf x:p\mathbf x=\mathbf 0\}$ is given by
\[\A[p]=\bigl(\tfrac np\ZZ/n\ZZ\bigr)^d.\]

\item The map $\mathbf x=\tfrac np\,\mathbf
y\mapsto\mathbf y\bmod p$ is an isomorphism $\A[p]\cong\FF_p^d$ of
$\FF_p$-vector spaces. 

\item Under this isomorphism, 

$\bullet \;$ elements of order $p$ correspond to
nonzero vectors; 

$\bullet \;$ cyclic subgroups of order $p$ correspond to lines, and
their number is $\gaussbinom d1_p=(p^d-1)/(p-1)$; 

$\bullet \;$ for a set $J$ of
order-$p$ cyclic subgroups, \[|\langle\bigcup J\rangle|=p^{\rk J},\] where
$\rk J$ is the dimension of the span of the corresponding lines.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
items.summary: Lemma 3.3 is one paper sentence with six claims, frozen as six Props: `torsionEqStatement` (𝒜[p] = ((n/p)ℤ/nℤ)^d as sets), `torsionIsoStatement` (the formula x = (n/p)y ↦ y mod p determines `torsionCoord`, and `torsionCoord` restricted to 𝒜[p] is an additive isomorphism onto 𝔽_p^d), `torsionOrderStatement` (order-p elements ↔ nonzero vectors), `torsionLinesStatement` (C ↦ lineOf C is a bijection 𝓛_p → lines, compatible with the isomorphism), `torsionCountStatement` (|𝓛_p| = [d 1]_p and = (p^d−1)/(p−1), in ℚ) and `torsionJoinStatement` (|⟨⋃J⟩| = p^{rk J}). `torsionLemmaStatement` is their conjunction.
deltas: Standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1 (Definition 2.1); 'Let p ∣ n be prime' = `p.Prime → p ∣ n`. No alphabet appears.
p𝐱 = `p • x` (ℕ-scalar multiplication on `Fin d → ZMod n`); 𝒜[p] = `latTorsion n d p`, whose carrier is literally `{v | p • v = 0}`.
((n/p)ℤ/nℤ)^d is rendered as the set of x whose every coordinate is the residue of some integer (n/p)·y; n/p is ℕ-division, exact since p ∣ n.

The paper's map 𝐱 = (n/p)𝐲 ↦ 𝐲 mod p is realised by `torsionCoord` (canonical representative val(x_i)/(n/p)); that it agrees with y mod p for EVERY integer representation x = (n/p)y is the first conjunct of `torsionIsoStatement`.
'Isomorphism of 𝔽_p-vector spaces' is an `AddEquiv` 𝒜[p] ≃+ (Fin d → ZMod p): 𝒜[p] has no ZMod p-module instance; additive maps between 𝔽_p-spaces are automatically 𝔽_p-linear, so nothing is lost.

'Correspond' is made concrete: order-p elements lie in 𝒜[p] and have order p iff their image is nonzero; C ↦ lineOf C (𝔽_p-span of the image of C ∩ 𝒜[p]) is a `Set.BijOn` from 𝓛_p onto the finrank-1 submodules, and x ∈ C ↔ torsionCoord x ∈ lineOf C on 𝒜[p].
𝓛_p = `orderPCyc n d p` (cyclic: C = zmultiples g for some g; order p: Nat.card C = p).
The count is stated in ℚ, against the paper's product definition `gaussProd` of [d 1]_p and against (p^d−1)/(p−1) separately (chain a = b = c as a = b ∧ a = c).
rk J = finrank of ⨆_{C∈J} lineOf C (the span of the lines = their join); J is any subset of 𝓛_p, J = ∅ included.

\begin{lemma}[Completeness]\label{lem:completeness} For any prime $p$, let $\mathcal L_p$ be the set of cyclic subgroups of order $p$ of $\A$ and let
$\mathcal L=\bigcup_{p\mid n}\mathcal L_p$. Then
\[S_{n^d}=\bigcup_{C\in\mathcal L}\Fix(C).\]
\end{lemma}

The union over 𝓛 = ⋃_{p∣n} 𝓛_p is flattened into a double union indexed by the prime p and C ∈ 𝓛_p.

items.label: lem:mobius
items.tex:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:mobius}
Let $p$ be prime, $d\ge1$, and $V\le\FF_p^d$ a subspace of dimension $r$,
with $\mathrm{lines}(V)$ its set of $1$-dimensional subspaces. Define 
\[f(V)\;:=\!\!\sum_{\substack{J\subseteq\mathrm{lines}(V)\\
  \operatorname{span}J=V}}\!\!(-1)^{|J|}
\]
Then
\[
  f(V)\;=\;\mu(0,V)\;=\;(-1)^r p^{\binom r2},
\]
where $\mu$ is the M\"obius function of the subspace lattice
\cite[Ex.~3.10.2]{stanley2012}.
\end{lemma}
items.summary: Lemma 4.1 is frozen as two Props in Paper/S03_MobiusCoefficients.lean: `lemMobiusFEqMuStatement` (f(V) = μ(0,V), with μ mathlib's incidence-algebra Möbius function on the subspace lattice of 𝔽_p^d) and `lemMobiusMuClosedFormStatement` (μ(0,V) = (−1)^r p^C(r,2)). Up to paper v7 the lemma also contained eq. (cr), which v8 states as Lemma 4.2 (lem_mobius2.json); the frozen conjunction `lemMobiusStatement` joins all three. lines(V) and span J are literal project definitions in the same file.
deltas: 𝔽_p^d = `Fin d → ZMod p`; subspace = `Submodule (ZMod p) _`; dimension = `Module.finrank (ZMod p)`; the zero subspace 0 = ⊥.

μ = mathlib's `IncidenceAlgebra.mu ℤ` on the whole lattice `Submodule (ZMod p) (Fin d → ZMod p)` (scoped Fintype/LocallyFiniteOrder instances; the latter is a Subsingleton, so the choice is immaterial).
The chain f(V) = μ(0,V) = (−1)^r p^C(r,2) is two separate Props with identical hypotheses; dim V = r is kept verbatim in the first even though it is unused there.

items.summary: Theorem 4.7 is frozen in Paper/S13_AbelianGroups.lean (group 13) as `abelianEnumStatement`: for a finite abelian group G (a type with `[AddCommGroup G] [Finite G]`) and σ ≥ 1, |S_G| cast to ℤ equals `abelianRHS (Nat.card G) (pRank G) σ`, the paper's sum re-indexed by the divisors h ≠ 1 of R = ∏_{p∣N} p^{d_p} (`rankRad`), as the core's `enumerationRHS` is for Theorem 4.4. Unlike Theorem 4.4 (bridge `P04.rankVectorReindexStatement`), no frozen Prop transcribes the vector-indexed sum for general G: the re-indexing v ↦ h = ∏ p^{v_p} has to be checked by reading `abelianRHS` and `coeffA`. The setting paragraph is covered by `pRank` + `pRankPowStatement` (the p-rank), `pTorsionVectorSpaceStatement` (G[p] is an F_p-vector space of dimension d_p), `rectCardStatement` and `rectRankStatement` (rectangular tori; the instance of the theorem is `rectEnumStatement`). The last sentence ('this is Theorem 4.4') is `squareStatement` (right sides agree) with `bridgeStatement` (the shift-symmetry predicates agree). Proofs: Paper/Proofs/P13_AbelianGroups*.lean, checked by AuditPaper (group 13).
deltas: Alphabet Σ = `Fin σ`; a finite abelian group is a type with `[AddCommGroup G] [Finite G]` (any universe), N = `Nat.card G`; |S_G| = `Nat.card` of the subtype of `IsShiftSymmetricG` configurations G → Fin σ, cast to ℤ (the right side has signs).

Shift-symmetric: `IsShiftSymmetricG s` := ∃ v ≠ 0, ∀ u, s (u + v) = s u (the paper's (τ_v s)(u) = s(u+v), i.e. Stab(s) ≠ {0}); stabilizers are not formalized separately. On ℤ_n^d it is the core's `IsShiftSymmetric` (`bridgeStatement`).

p-rank: `pRank G p` is the exponent of p in |G[p]|; `pRankPowStatement` certifies |G[p]| = p^{pRank G p} for prime p, and `pTorsionVectorSpaceStatement` (group-13 supplement, 2026-11-08) certifies that G[p] is an F_p-vector space (ZMod p acting naturally) of dimension pRank G p.

The vector-indexed sum is re-indexed by the divisors h ≠ 1 of R = ∏_{p∣N} p^{d_p} (`rankRad`): v_p = v_p(h), |v| = Ω(h) (`bigOmega`), product over the primes of h only (r_{d_p}(p,0) = 1), as in the core's `enumerationRHS`. No frozen bridge to the vector-indexed form exists for general G (Theorem 4.4 has `P04.rankVectorReindexStatement`); on ℤ_n^d, `squareStatement` reduces it to `enumerationRHS`.

Exponents are ℕ-quotients N / h. Exact because h ∣ R ∣ N (p^{d_p} = |G[p]| divides N by Lagrange; helper `pRank_pow_dvd` in the proofs); unlike Theorem 4.4 (`exponentEncodingStatement`) no frozen Prop records the exactness.
Rectangular tori are `∀ i : Fin d, ZMod (n i)` with all n i ≥ 1 (ZMod 0 = ℤ); the paper's number of factors m is `d` here.

'this is Theorem 4.4' = the right sides agree (`squareStatement`, for n ≥ 1 and every d, σ) and the predicates agree (`bridgeStatement`, for every n, d, σ): both are stated more generally than Theorem 4.4's n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 1.

Not frozen: the opening sentence (a remark on the structure of a proof; its torsion fact is Lemma 3.3, `P02.torsionLemmaStatement`) and the proof. 'An F_p-vector space', listed as not frozen in the S13 docstring, is frozen in the group-13 supplement (`pTorsionVectorSpaceStatement`, Run 046).

items.label: thm:kactive
items.title: $k$-active enumeration
items.tex:
\begin{theorem}[$k$-active enumeration]\label{thm:kactive}
For all integers $n\ge2$, $d, \sigma\ge1$, and $0\le k\le N=n^d$, with
$h(\vv)=\prod_i p_i^{v_i}$, we have:
\[
  |S^a_{n^d,k}| \;=\; \sum_{\substack{\vv\in\{0,\dots,d\}^{\omega(n)}\\
  \vv\neq\mathbf 0}} (-1)^{1+|\vv|}\,\prod_{i=1}^{\omega(n)} r_d(p_i,v_i)\;
  \binom{\,N/h(\vv)\,}{\,k/h(\vv)\,}\,
  (\sigma-1)^{\,(N-k)/h(\vv)} .
\]
Note: To avoid a notational conflict with the active-cell
count $k$, the rank vectors here run over $\vv\in\{0,\dots,d\}^{\omega(n)}$,
with one coordinate per distinct prime factor.
\end{theorem}
items.summary: Theorem 5.1 is frozen as the single Prop `kActiveStatement`: for n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 1, k ≤ n^d and every state a : Fin σ, the integer cast of `numKActive n d σ a k` (= |S^a_{n^d,k}|) equals `kActiveRHS n d σ k`. The right-hand side is the sum of `kActiveSummand` over the nonzero rank vectors; the §5 binomial convention (annihilation of the whole summand unless k/h(v) is an integer in {0,…,N/h(v)}) is encoded as an `if … then … else 0` guard inside `kActiveSummand`, and the guard is proved equivalent to the paper's rational condition (`guard_iff`).
deltas: Alphabet Σ is `Fin σ` (only |Σ| = σ enters); the fixed state a is universally quantified after σ (the paper fixes a before the theorem); the right-hand side does not depend on a, as in the paper.
|S^a_{n^d,k}| is `numKActive` = `Nat.card` of the subtype of shift-symmetric configurations with `cellsInState s a = k`; the equation is stated in ℤ (the right-hand side is a signed sum).

Rank vectors are functions `n.primeFactors → ℕ` with values in {0,…,d} (`Fintype.piFinset … Finset.range (d + 1)`): coordinates are labelled by the prime p itself rather than by its index i in p_1 < ⋯ < p_{ω(n)}; v ≠ 0 is `.erase 0`.

r_d(p,v) is `rdCoeff p v d = p^{C(v,2)} · gaussBinom p d v`; `gaussBinom` is the q-Pascal recurrence, linked to the paper's product formula by the separately frozen and proved `ShiftSym.P01.gaussBinomProductFidelityStatement`.

§5 convention: the summand is `if h(v) ∣ k ∧ k/h(v) ≤ N/h(v) then … else 0` with ℕ-division; `guard_iff` proves this guard is exactly 'k/h(v) is an integer in {0,…,N/h(v)}' with rational quotients. Under k ≤ N the second conjunct is automatic once h(v) ∣ k.
N/h(v), k/h(v), (N−k)/h(v) are ℕ-divisions, exact: h(v) ∣ n^d (`hVec_dvd_pow`), h(v) ∣ k by the guard, and n^d − k is untruncated because k ≤ n^d is a hypothesis.
σ − 1 is computed in ℤ (no truncated subtraction); 0^0 = 1 is Lean's `pow_zero` (the paper's convention, relevant only at σ = 1, k = N).

The annihilation rule is applied only to binom(N/h(v), k/h(v)); the binom(v_i,2) inside r_d is the ordinary `Nat.choose` — exactly the v5 paper wording ('all other binomial coefficients are the ordinary ones'). The Lean docstrings still record a PAPER ISSUE about the scope of the convention as worded in v3.1 ('Here and below'); that wording has since been replaced in the paper by the restricted one, so the issue is resolved in v5.

maps.note: Equality in ℤ of the cast count and the frozen right-hand side.

maps.note: Same four hypotheses, as antecedents; 0 ≤ k is automatic for k : ℕ.

the rank vectors here run over $\vv\in\{0,\dots,d\}^{\omega(n)}$,

maps.note: Product over the distinct primes of n, in ℕ.

maps.note: ℕ-division, exact because h(v) ∣ n^d for every rank vector (`hVec_dvd_pow`, proved; the paper's 'Integrality' remark in the proof of Theorem 4.4).

maps.label: k/h(v)
maps.note: ℕ-division, exact in the then-branch since the guard contains h(v) ∣ k.

maps.note: Computed in ℤ, so no truncated ℕ-subtraction (it is 0 exactly at σ = 1).

maps.note: ℕ-subtraction is exact because k ≤ n^d (hypothesis); the ℕ-division is exact in the then-branch because h(v) divides both n^d and k.

maps.label: §5 convention: C(N/h,k/h) := 0 unless k/h ∈ {0,…,N/h} ∩ ℤ, annihilating the whole summand

whole summand

items.label: cor:prob
items.title: Uniform distribution
items.tex:
\begin{corollary}[Uniform distribution]\label{cor:prob}
For a configuration drawn uniformly from $\Sigma^{n^d}$, the probability
$P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{n^d}=|S_{n^d}|/\sigma^{n^d}$ satisfies
\[
    F_d(n,\sigma)\,\sigma^{-n^d}
    \;\le\; P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{n^d} \;\le\;
    \bigl(2^d-1+2\log_2 n\bigr)\,\sigma^{-n^d/2},
\]
where $F_d(n, \sigma)$ denotes the lower bound on $|S_{n^d}|$ given in Theorem~\ref{thm:lower-bound}.
So $P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{n^d}$ decays as $\sigma^{-cN}$ with
$N=n^d$ and decay rate
$c=\log_\sigma(1/P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{n^d})/N\in
[\tfrac12-o(1),\,1-\tfrac1{p_1}]$, where $p_1$ is the smallest prime
factor of $n$. The lower end is given by Theorem~\ref{thm:upper-bound}(ii), and the
upper end is the single-subgroup inclusion $\Fix(C)\subseteq S_{n^d}$ for
one order-$p_1$ cyclic subgroup $C$, which gives
$P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{n^d}\ge\sigma^{N/p_1-N}$ (this is also the lower bound
of Proposition~\ref{prop:rate}). Here $o(1)$ refers to any regime with
$N=n^d\to\infty$.
\end{corollary}
items.summary: Corollary 7.1 is frozen as the conjunction `probUnifCorollaryStatement` of seven Props: `probSandwichStatement` (both real inequalities), `decayIdentityStatement` (P = σ^{−cN}), `decayIntervalStatement` = `decayLowerUniformStatement` (uniform ε–M form of c ≥ 1/2 − o(1)) ∧ `decayUpperStatement` (c ≤ 1 − 1/p₁), `decayLowerExplicitStatement` (c ≥ 1/2 − log_σ K/N), `singleSubgroupStatement`, `probSingleLowerStatement` (P ≥ σ^{N/p₁−N}), and `probSingleLowerIsRateLowerStatement` (the parenthetical as a per-instance ↔). P^unif is `probUnif = |S|/σ^{n^d}` in ℝ and c is `decayRate`.
deltas: Standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2 (Definition 2.1) are explicit antecedents of every part; the corollary itself states none.
P^unif is defined as the real number |S_{n^d}|/σ^{n^d} (`probUnif`); the uniform distribution is not modelled as a measure.
F_d(n,σ) is `lowerEnvelope` (q-Pascal binomials at q = n, an integer, cast to ℝ); equal to the paper's product-formula F_d by `envelopeIntegralStatement`.
σ^{−n^d}, σ^{−n^d/2}, σ^{N/p₁−N}, σ^{−cN} are real powers (`Real.rpow`) of σ > 0; log₂ = `Real.logb 2`, log_σ = `Real.logb σ`.
p₁ = `Nat.minFac n`.
'decays as σ^{−cN}' is the exact identity P = σ^{−cN} (true by the definition of c, given P > 0).
'c ≥ 1/2 − o(1) in any regime with N → ∞' is the uniform statement ∀ε>0 ∃M ∀(n,d,σ) with n^d ≥ M: c ≥ 1/2 − ε (implies every regime; uniform also in σ).

The single-subgroup Prop adds the count |Fix(C)| = σ^{N/p₁} as a conjunct (implicit in 'which gives').
'(this is also the lower bound of Proposition 10.1)' is read as the per-instance equivalence of P ≥ σ^{N/p₁−N} with σ^{N/p₁} ≤ |S_{n^d}|.

items.title: Insolvability
items.tex:
\begin{corollary}[Insolvability]\label{cor:insolv}
Let $\sigma\ge2$ and $N>1$. Any task requiring, on some input, an output
configuration outside $S_{n^d}$ reachable from an input inside $S_{n^d}$
is unsolvable by translation-equivariant CA on $\ZZ_n^d$. Indeed, symmetric inputs
exist (all constants lie in $S_{n^d}$), and by Theorem~\ref{thm:irrev} no
trajectory leaves $S_{n^d}$. This covers leader election
(the target configuration with a unique distinguished cell is asymmetric
for $N>1$); $d$-dimensional
leader-election algorithms as in \cite{nichitiu1999,stratmann2002}
therefore necessarily
break one of the hypotheses (uniformity, determinism, synchrony) or
restrict the admissible inputs, e.g.\ to asymmetric configurations.
More generally, since $\Stab$ can only grow along a trajectory
(Theorem~\ref{thm:irrev}), every pattern-recognition or image-processing
task whose required output breaks a symmetry of some admissible input is
unsolvable, as in the two-dimensional discussion of \cite{banda2019}.
\end{corollary}
items.summary: Corollary 8.2 is split into eight frozen Props, conjoined in `insolvStatement`: the general unsolvability claim (for equivariant maps, `insolvGeneralStatement`, and for offset CA, `insolvGeneralCAStatement`), the two justifications inside the corollary (constants are symmetric; no trajectory leaves S), the leader-election claims (targets asymmetric, never reached, the task unsolvable) and the closing sentence's mathematical core (`leaderRestrictStatement`: an equivariant solver must avoid every symmetric input). The paper does not define 'task' or 'solvable'; Lean introduces `Task`, `Solves`, `RequiresLeavingS`, `leaderTask`, `leaderTaskOn` for this. The paper has no proof environment; `insolv_proved` certifies the frozen type. Since 2026-10-27 the symmetry-breaking sentence (added in v5, reworded in v7) is frozen in the group-07 supplement `S07_Dynamics_SymmetryBreaking.lean`: `insolvSymBreakStatement`, with the hypothesis `RequiresSymmetryBreaking` (on some admissible input every acceptable output breaks a symmetry of it), and `insolvFullStatement` = `insolvStatement` ∧ `insolvSymBreakStatement`.
deltas: The paper does not define 'task': a `Task` is a set of admissible inputs plus, for each input, a set of acceptable outputs (the most general input/output specification).

'Solvable' = `Solves`: from every admissible input the trajectory reaches an acceptable output at SOME step k ≥ 0 (no halting, no stay requirement) — the weakest success notion, so its negation is the strongest unsolvability.
'Requiring, on some input, an output outside S reachable from an input inside S' = `RequiresLeavingS`: some admissible input x ∈ S ALL of whose acceptable outputs lie outside S.
'Translation-equivariant CA' = any map with `Equivariant Φ` (general form), and separately the offset CA `caMap offs φ` of Definition 2.4 (any b, including b = 0).
N > 1 is written `1 < n ^ d`; σ ≥ 2 and N > 1 are kept as stated but are not used by the implications (they make the situation non-degenerate).
'Unique distinguished cell' = some state occupies exactly one cell (the leader state is not fixed in advance).
Leader election (as a task) = all inputs admissible, acceptable outputs = exactly one cell in the leader state ℓ, others arbitrary.

The closing sentence is formalized in its contrapositive: an equivariant (uniform, deterministic, synchronous) solver of leader election on inputs X must have X ∩ S = ∅ — the paper's own example ('restrict ... to asymmetric configurations'), a disclosed strengthening of the literal 'restrict the admissible inputs'.

'Every pattern-recognition or image-processing task whose required output breaks a symmetry of some admissible input' = `RequiresSymmetryBreaking` for EVERY task (the informal task names are not formalized: a generalization). 'Breaks a symmetry' = some translation fixing the input does not fix the output (¬ stab x ≤ stab y), the largest true reading; it is strictly more than `RequiresLeavingS`.

items.title: Per-prime rank monotonicity
items.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Per-prime rank monotonicity]\label{prop:rank}
For a prime $p\mid n$ define the \emph{$p$-rank} of $\ssb$ as
$\rk_p(\ssb)=\dim_{\FF_p}\bigl(\Stab(\ssb)\cap\A[p]\bigr)\in\{0,\dots,d\}$
(via Lemma~\ref{lem:torsion}). Under any translation-equivariant $\Phi$,
every $p$-rank is non-decreasing along every trajectory:
$\rk_p(\Phi(\ssb))\ge\rk_p(\ssb)$ for all $p\mid n$ simultaneously.
\end{proposition}
items.summary: Proposition 8.3 is frozen as five Props conjoined in `rankStatement`: the range claim of the definition (`rankRangeStatement`, rk_p ∈ {0,…,d}), one-step monotonicity for all primes p | n (`rankMonoStatement`), monotonicity along trajectories (`rankTrajStatement`), and two Lean-only well-definedness anchors of the definition of rk_p (`rankCardStatement`: |Stab(s) ∩ A[p]| = p^{rk_p(s)}; `rankIntrinsicStatement`: rk_p does not depend on the Lemma 3.3 isomorphism). The p-rank itself is the definition `rkP`: the F_p-dimension of the image of Stab(s) ∩ A[p] under the Lemma 3.3 isomorphism A[p] ≅ F_p^d.
deltas: rk_p = `rkP`: `Module.finrank (ZMod p)` of the F_p-submodule (`AddSubgroup.toZModSubmodule`) that is the image of Stab(s) ∩ A[p] under `latTorsionEquiv` (the Lemma 3.3 isomorphism A[p] ≅ F_p^d) — 'via Lemma 3.3' taken literally.

Two extra Props pin the definition down independently of that isomorphism: |Stab(s) ∩ A[p]| = p^{rk_p(s)}, and rk_p = finrank of Stab(s) ∩ A[p] with its own ZMod p-module structure. They are not paper claims.
'Prime p | n' = hypotheses `p.Prime`, `p ∣ n`; the proofs `hn : 2 ≤ n` are named because `rkP` needs n ≠ 0 (`by omega`).
{0,…,d} = `Finset.Icc 0 d`.
'Non-decreasing along every trajectory' = `Monotone (k ↦ rk_p(Φ^[k] s))`; 'for all p | n simultaneously' = the prime is quantified after Φ and s are fixed.

\begin{proposition}[Average case, uniform random input]
\label{prop:detect-avg}

subgroup, run on its own, visits in expectation exactly

\]
\end{proposition}

items.display: Proposition 10.1 (Decay-rate law: only the smallest prime factor survives)
items.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Decay-rate law: only the smallest prime factor
survives]\label{prop:rate}
Let $p_1=p_1(n)$ be the smallest prime factor of $n$ and $N=n^d$. For all
$n\ge2$, $d\ge1$, $\sigma\ge2$:
\[
    \sigma^{N/p_1}\;\le\;|S_{n^d}|\;\le\;
    2\log_2(n)\,n^{d-1}\,\sigma^{N/p_1}.
\]
Consequently the decay rate $c(n,d):=-\log_\sigma
P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{n^d}/N$ satisfies
\[
    0\;\le\;\Bigl(1-\frac1{p_1}\Bigr)-c(n,d)\;\le\;
    \frac{\log_\sigma\bigl(2\,n^{d-1}\log_2 n\bigr)}{N}
    \;\xrightarrow[d\to\infty]{}\;0 ,
\]
so $c(n,d)\to1-1/p_1(n)$. Asymptotically in $d$, lattice sides fall into
\emph{universality classes} determined solely by their smallest prime
factor, with even $n$ on the extremal class $c=1/2$ (the floor permitted
by Theorem~\ref{thm:upper-bound}) and primes $p$ on $c=1-1/p$.
\end{proposition}

items.title: Inversion law
items.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Inversion law]\label{prop:inversion}
Let $p\ge3$ be prime, $\sigma\ge2$, and set
$\varphi(d)=(1-\tfrac1p)\,p^d-\tfrac12(p+1)^d$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item if $\varphi(d)>\log_\sigma\bigl(2\log_2(p)\,p^{d-1}\bigr)$, then
$P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{(p+1)^d}>P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{p^d}$ (composite
advantage);
\item if $\varphi(d)<-\log_\sigma\bigl(2\log_2(p{+}1)\,(p{+}1)^{d-1}\bigr)$,
then $P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{(p+1)^d}<P^{\mathrm{unif}}_{p^d}$ (prime
advantage).
\end{enumerate}
The function $\varphi$, regarded as a function of real $d$, is positive
below and negative above its unique zero
\[
    d_c(p)\;=\;\frac{\ln\bigl(2-\tfrac2p\bigr)}{\ln\bigl(1+\tfrac1p\bigr)}
    \;=\;p\ln2+O(1)\qquad(p\to\infty),
\]
so the two-dimensional ``composite advantage'' inverts within an
explicitly bounded window around $d_c(p)$, a dimension that grows
\emph{linearly} in the prime: (i) applies to every integer $d\ge1$ with
$d\le d_c(p)-20$, and (ii) to every integer $d\ge d_c(p)+20$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Union interpretation on rectangular tori]\label{lem:dtorus}
Let $1\le m<k$ and $1\le j\le d$. Then
\[
  0\;\le\;q^m(p^{-j})\;\le\;\sigma^{N_j},
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  q^m(p^{-1})\;\le\;\sum_{i\le m}\gaussbinom d1_{p_i}\,\sigma^{N_1/p_i}.
\]
\end{lemma}
items.summary: Lemma A.1 is frozen as two Props: the sandwich 0 ≤ q^m(p^{-j}) ≤ σ^{N_j} is `lemA1SandwichStatement`, the union bound at j = 1 is `lemA1UnionBoundStatement`; `lemA1Statement` is their conjunction. q^m(c) is the literal real-valued truncation `qTrunc` (real power `Real.rpow` with exponent c·n^d·∏ p_i^{-v_i}), p = p_{m+1} is `primeAt n m` (0-indexed increasing list of prime factors), N_j is the real number `Nj n d p j = n^d/p^j`. The title's 'union interpretation' (q^m(p^{−j}) counts the configurations of T_j fixed by some order-p_i subgroup) is a step of the proof, frozen as the auxiliary `unionInterpretationStatement`; it is not part of the lemma's statement.

q^m(c) is `qTrunc n d σ m c : ℝ`, with v ∈ {0,…,d}^m as `v : Fin m → Fin (d+1)`, the power of σ as `Real.rpow` with real exponent c·n^d·∏ p_i^{-v_i} (zpow), no rounding.

\begin{lemma}[Coefficient estimates]\label{lem:coef}
Let $q\ge2$ be real, with $\gaussbinom dj_q$ and
$r_d(q,j)=q^{\binom j2}\gaussbinom dj_q$ defined by the product formula.
Then $\gaussbinom dj_q\le 4q^{\,j(d-j)}$,
$\gaussbinom d1_q\le 2q^{\,d-1}$, and
$\sum_{j=2}^{d}r_d(q,j)\le 4(d-1)\,q^{D}$.
\end{lemma}

items.title: Dependence on the ranks
items.tex:
\begin{corollary}[Dependence on the ranks]\label{cor:abelian-ranks}
Let $\sigma\ge2$, and write $\mathrm{ac}(G)=\sigma^{|G|}-|S_G|$ for the number of
aperiodic configurations.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $|S_G|$ depends on $G$ only through $N$ and its $p$-ranks; for
example, $\ZZ_2\times\ZZ_{24}$ and $\ZZ_4\times\ZZ_{12}$ both have $50\,388\,256$
shift-symmetric configurations for $\sigma=2$.
\item If $G'$ has the same order as $G$, $d_p(G')=d_p(G)+1$ for one prime
$p$, and the other ranks agree, then
$|S_{G'}|-|S_G|=p^{d_p(G)}\,\mathrm{ac}(G'')>0$ for any abelian group $G''$ of
order $N/p$ with the ranks of $G$. In particular, among the abelian groups
of order $N$, the cyclic group has the fewest shift-symmetric
configurations.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
items.summary: Corollary 4.8 is frozen as five Props of group 13 (Paper/S13_AbelianGroups.lean). (i): `onlyRanksStatement` (two finite abelian groups with the same order and the same p-rank at every prime have the same |S|; for every σ) and `cardTwoPrimeStatement` (the example). (ii): `monotoneStatement` (the identity |S_{G'}| − |S_G| = p^{d_p(G)} ac(G'') in ℤ and ac(G'') > 0, for every supplied G'' of order N/p with the ranks of G), `stepStrictStatement` (|S_G| < |S_{G'}| with no G'' supplied) and `cyclicMinStatement` (|S_{ℤ_N}| ≤ |S_G|: 'the fewest' read as attaining the minimum; that the cyclic group is the unique minimizer is NOT certified). ac is not a Lean definition; it is written out inside `monotoneStatement`. The proof (q-Pascal, existence of G'') is not audited.
deltas: Groups are types with `[AddCommGroup _] [Finite _]`, alphabet `Fin σ`, |S_G| = `Nat.card` of the `IsShiftSymmetricG` configurations, d_p(G) = `pRank G p` (see the item of Theorem 4.7).
σ ≥ 2 is kept in (ii) (`monotoneStatement`, `stepStrictStatement`, `cyclicMinStatement`); (i) (`onlyRanksStatement`) is stated for every σ; the example fixes σ = 2.
'depends on G only through N and its p-ranks' is read as: equal order and equal p-rank at every prime imply equal counts (equality in ℕ).
ac(H) = σ^{|H|} − |S_H| is not a Lean definition: it is written out in ℤ inside `monotoneStatement` (only ac(G'') occurs). That it counts the aperiodic configurations is not frozen.
G'' of order N/p is `Nat.card G'' * p = Nat.card G` (no ℕ-division); 'the ranks of G' are compared at every prime (S13 docstring Delta).

The strict increase is frozen twice: 0 < ac(G'') for a supplied G'' (`monotoneStatement`), and |S_G| < |S_{G'}| with no G'' supplied (`stepStrictStatement`; the existence of G'' is part of what is certified). The existence of G'' itself is not a frozen Prop.

'the cyclic group has the fewest': the cyclic group of order N = `Nat.card G` is `ZMod N`; read as |S_{ℤ_N}| ≤ |S_G| for every finite abelian G (attaining the minimum). Uniqueness of the minimizer is neither claimed by the text (S13 docstring reading) nor certified.
The example groups are `∀ i : Fin 2, ZMod (![2, 8] i)` and `∀ i : Fin 2, ZMod (![4, 4] i)` (the rectangular form); alphabet `Fin 2`.
